title: inspect-and-serialize-sse-fragments-to-avoid-midjson-shifts
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes: Fixes rare cases where SSE chunk boundaries split JSON tokens or tool-call markers, causing partial JSON emissions and fncall ordering issues. Adds a fragment inspector and deterministic mux serialization to improve stream stability.
description: Context: We still observed customer incidents where SSE streams emitted partial JSON objects when TCP/chunk boundaries bisected UTF-8 sequences or JSON tokens, and in edge cases interleaved tool/function-call sentinel frames were reordered by the mux during concurrent writes. Motivation: reduce customer-facing partial-json errors and fncall ordering regressions without large changes to the public streaming API. Changes: 1) Introduce a lightweight fragment_inspector component in the serving runtime that classifies incoming byte slices for safe emission: UTF-8 tail-finding, JSON token boundary hints, and a small checksum to detect replays. 2) Add a serialization shim in the sse_mux that serializes fragments using an ordinal stamped at the sender and enforces per-stream in-order flush guarantees for fncall/tool sentinel frames. 3) When a mid-json split is detected, the inspector will coalesce contiguous pending fragments up to a safe window or emit an escaped placeholder and enqueue a soft-resume marker; this avoids spurious partial JSON objects. 4) OpenAI-compat layer updates: ensure function-call sentinel objects are emitted as atomic events with a trailing zero-length field when serialized to SSE to make downstream parsers deterministic. 5) Add unit and integration tests including a deterministic replay harness and a small fuzz runner that simulates network chunking patterns encountered in production. Checklist: - [x] Add fragment_inspector implementation and tests; - [x] Add sse_mux serialization shim and tests; - [x] Update openai_compat emitter to append atomic sentinel framing; - [x] Add integration test that reproduces previously-reported mid-json incident; - [x] Run existing SSE compatibility suite and fix fallout. Commits: summary of 5 commits included: "fragment inspector + unit tests", "sse mux serializer and ordering enforcement", "openai_compat: atomic sentinel framing", "integration reproducer and regression test", "test harness and CI config for chunk-fuzzing". Files touched (high level): runtime/sse/fragment_inspector.rs, runtime/sse/mux_serializer.rs, openai_compat/stream_emitter.go, sdk/python/streaming_client.py, tests/integration/sse_midjson_repro.test, tests/fuzz/chunk_harness.go, ci/flakeguard.yml, docs/streaming_stability.md. Risk/regressions: small latency increase (microseconds) under extreme write fanout due to ordinal stamping; mitigated by batching path and configurable window. Performance: added microbenchmarks show median tail-latency unchanged for normal workloads and 0.6-1.4% increased CPU in worst-case synthetic stress tests. Why this approach: prior heuristic fixes addressed many delimiter issues but left a class of boundary/ordering races; explicit inspection + deterministic serialization is simpler to reason about and is easier to test and reason about during canary rollouts. Migration: default enabled; runtime flag sse.fragment_inspector=on to disable in emergencies. Merge: approved by reviewers after 2 rounds of small fixes; CI green; merged by squash.
